Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle. Quezon City TIME-: http: /tww•w. dilg_gov.ph otLG OPtNlON NO. LC 06 JUN ATTY. CERILIO NEIL E. PACANA Provincial Legal Officer Province of Misamis Oriental Dear Atty. Pacana: This has reference to your letter dated 18 October 2017 requesting for this Department's legal opinion on the issue of whether or not the Local School Board (ISB) of Misamis Oriental may provide assistance to construct a multi-purpose room/laboratory in favor of Tagoloan Community College, a tertiary school owned by the Municipal Government of Taoloan, to be financed by the Special Education Fund (SEF). In your letter, you inquired if the above-mentioned construction of a multi-purpose room/laboratory in Tagoloan Community College (TCC) can be funded under the SEF, and that, the said project will be used exclusively for the senior high school program. Be it noted that under Section 4 of Republic Act No. 105331, Secondary education refers to the third stage of compulsory basic education. It consists of four (4) years of junior high school education and two (2) years of senior high school. The entrant age to the junior and senior high school levels are typically twelve (12) and sixteen (16) years old, respectively. In reply to your above query, may we invite your attention to the provision of the DepEd-DBM-DILG Joint Circular (JC) No. I, dated 19 January 2017, particularly Item 4.0 on the Allowable Expenses Chargeable Against the SEF, to wit: "4.1.2 Construction and repair of school buildings: 4.1.2. I Construction, repair and maintenance of school buildings and other facilities for public elementary and secondary schools, which are deemed to ha ve shortage of classrooms or of other facilities, as the case may be, per DepEd classroom deployment analysis, subject to existing standar&specifications set by DepEd and/or Department of Public Works and Highways; furthermore, this item shall be given priority in the SEF Budget; (Emphasis supplied) " Enhanced Basic Education Act of 2013

Likewise, Sections 100(c)(1) and 272 of the Local Government Code (LGC) provides that: "SECTION 100. (c) The annual school board budget shall give priority to the following: (I) Construction, repair, and maintenance of school buildings and other facilities of public elementary and secondary schools; and SECTION 272. Application of Proceeds of the Additional One Percent SEF Tax. - The proceeds from the additional one percent (1%) tax on real property accruing to the Special Education Fund (SEF) shall be automatically released to the local school boards: Provided, That, in case of provinces, the proceeds shall be divided equally between the provincial and municipal school boards: Provided, however, That the proceeds shall be allocated for the operation and maintenance of public schools, construction and repair of school buildings, facilities and equipment, educational research, purchase of books and periodicals, and sports development as determined and approved by the Local School Board. " On the basis of the above-quoted provision of the issuance and law, this Department believes that the proposed construction of a multi-purpose room/laboratory in favor of a tertiary school even if it will be used exclusively by the senior high school cannot be funded under the SEF as Item 4.1.2.1 of the DepEd-DBM-DILG Joint Circular (JC) No. 1, S.2017 and Section I of the LGC explicitly provides that the allowable expenses chargeable against the SEF is for the construction of school buildings and other facilities in favor of public elementary and secondary schools. Moreover, although it is provided in Section 4 of RA No. 10533 that senior high school education is still part of the secondary education, and that, the said project will be used exclusively by the senior high school students, we are of the considered view that since the location of the said project is within TCC, still the SEF cannot be utilized for that purpose. The law and the issuance mentioned-above are very clear that said construction should be in favor of public elementary and secondary schools. It would have been different, we believe, if what is provided therein is the construction of school buildings in favor of a public elementary and secondary students.

Accordingly, since the above-mentioned issuance and law are very clear, the SEF should not be utilized for the construction of a multi-purpose hall/laboratory in favor of a tertiary/college school as the same is contrary to the provisions of the LGC. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, By Auth y of the Secretary: AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary
